> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/c7deeb3e-3110-567c-bdbd-2d0511efaf01)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

A building has `n` meeting rooms, labeled `0` through `n - 1`. Implement `mostBooked(n, meetings)`, where `meetings` holds `m` entries and `meetings[i] = [start_i, end_i]` gives the start and end times at which meeting `i` was originally planned.

Rooms are assigned according to these rules:

1. A meeting is placed in the free room whose index is lowest.
2. When every room is occupied at the moment a meeting is supposed to start, the meeting is pushed back until the first room frees up, and it keeps the same length it was planned to have.
3. When more than one room frees up at the same moment, the room with the lowest index is the one used.
4. Meetings are handled in increasing order of their originally planned start times; no two meetings share the same `start_i`.

Return the index of the room in which the largest number of meetings took place. If several rooms tie for that count, return the lowest index among them.

Example 1:

```text
Input: n = 2, meetings = [[0,10],[1,5],[2,7],[3,4]]

Output: 0
```

Explanation: Meeting `[0,10]` takes room `0` and `[1,5]` takes room `1`. Meeting `[2,7]` must wait until room `1` frees at time `5`, running over `[5,10]`. Meeting `[3,4]` waits until time `10`, when both rooms free simultaneously, so it goes to room `0` over `[10,11]`. Each room hosts two meetings, and the tie goes to room `0`.

Example 2:

```text
Input: n = 3, meetings = [[0,10],[1,9],[2,8],[3,7],[4,6]]

Output: 1
```

Explanation: The first three meetings take rooms `0`, `1` and `2`. Meeting `[3,7]` finds every room busy and waits for room `2`, which frees at time `8`, so it runs `[8,12]`. Meeting `[4,6]` then waits for room `1`, which frees at time `9`, and runs `[9,11]`. Room `0` hosted one meeting while rooms `1` and `2` hosted two each, so the tie is broken toward room `1`.

Example 3:

```text
Input: n = 4, meetings = [[0,2],[3,5],[6,8]]

Output: 0
```

Explanation: Every meeting starts when room `0` is already free, so room `0` hosts all three meetings and no other room is used.

Constraints:

* $$1 \le n \le 100$$
* $$1 \le m \le 100{,}000$$, where `m` is the length of `meetings`
* $$0 \le start_i < end_i \le 500{,}000$$
* Every `start_i` is distinct.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Simulate the meetings in order of original start time, and think about what you need to know at each moment: which rooms are free and when the busy ones finish.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use one min-heap of free room indices and another min-heap of (end time, room) for busy rooms, moving rooms back to the free heap as their end times pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

When no room is free, take the busy room with the earliest end time (lowest index on ties) and delay the meeting by keeping its duration, use 64-bit values for times and count usage per room.

</details>
